did.unittitle: American Society of International Law records

physdesc.extent: 169 containers: 163 letter document boxes, 5 legal document boxes, 1 half-letter document box.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The American Society of International Law records document the governance, programming, publications, and institutional development of ASIL. The collection includes extensive materials created by the Executive Council and Executive Committee, such as meeting minutes, agendas, correspondence, and planning documents that reflect the Society's leadership and strategic direction over time. The records also document ASIL's grant-seeking activities and funded initiatives, including proposals, reports, and communications with major philanthropic organizations such as the MacArthur Foundation, Mellon Foundation, and United States Institute of Peace. These materials illustrate ASIL's efforts to advance international legal scholarship, outreach, and education. Additional series cover the Society's interest groups, annual meetings, editorial boards, and flagship publications, the American Journal of International Law and International Legal Materials. The collection also includes printed materials, photographs, digital files, and historical documentation that provide insight into ASIL's public engagement, institutional memory, and evolving priorities.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into series that reflect the functional and organizational structure of the American Society of International Law (ASIL), preserving original order when evident. The series include: Series 1: Executive Council and Executive Committee Files Series 2: General Files Series 3: Grant Domains Series 4: Interest Groups Series 5: American Journal of International Law (AJIL) Series 5.1: Board of Editors Series 6: International Legal Materials (ILM) Series 7: Annual Meetings – Programs Series 8: Annual Meetings – Planning Series 9: Brochures and Printed Material Series 10: Event Files Series 11: ASIL History Series 12: Photographs Series 13: Digital and Audiovisual Materials

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Open for research. RAC provides an access surrogate of digital media and born-digital files, not the original files. To request an access surrogate be made, please contact a RAC archivist. When requesting to view audiovisual material, please check the "Access" note for each Title. If a Title does not currently have an access copy, please contact a RAC archivist for further instruction. All inquiries to view motion picture film require advanced notice of at least 2 business days, and may necessitate notice of up to one week.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: This collection was donated to RAC by the American Society of International Law in 2024.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Labelled "just for kicks of interest generally to the Society. Scan/save as you'd like." Includes: correspondence with Imperial German Consul; James Scott to George Wilson re: late AJIL submission; letter stating policy banning women from society banquets but allowing women to attend society meetings, and correspondence re: suspending ASIL annual meetings for 1918, 1919, and 1920.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Materials pulled for scanning by staff. Includes: 50th, 54th, and 55th annual meeting programs, invitation to Dr. Tsunejiro Miyaoka to join the ASIL Executive Committee, correspondence re: invitations to join ASIL, the Extraterritoriality Report, annual meetings, Charles S. Lobingier correspondence, letter from Chinese National Welfare Society in America re: "Shantung territory" (Shandong) and support from the United States (1919). Also included is ASIL's constitution, the creation of the School of International Relations at Johns Hopkins University by the Committee of Resolutions, Franklin D. Roosevelt (1924), letter to Robert Lansing (1915), correspondence with William H. Taft (1915), and a preliminary membership to the International Law Association of America following the Lake Mohonk meeting (1905).
